summary: K. T. S. Sarao works in Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at DAV College, Panjab University, the University of Delhi, and the University of Cambridge under Raymond Allchin and Kenneth Roy Norman, becoming a professor at Delhi in 1995.

K. V. Puttappa (1904–1994) worked in linguistics and other fields. He was educated at Hardwick High School and College, Maharaja's College, Mysore (around 1923–1927), and the University of Mysore (around 1927–1929), later teaching T. V. Venkatachala Sastry.

K. V. Raman (1934–2024) was an Indology and archaeology scholar. He studied at Madras Christian College under A. J. Boyd, the University of Madras, and the Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya Institute, later serving at the ASI and the University of Madras.

K. V. Ramesh (1935–2013) was a scholar in Indology, history, and archaeology. He served as Director at the Archaeological Survey of India (attested 1986–1987), Honorary Director at the Oriental Research Institute Mysore (attested 2012), and Secretary of the Epigraphical Society.
K. V. Rangaswami Aiyangar (1880–1960) was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. Around 1935 to 1939, he served as Principal at Banaras Hindu University and Central Hindu College.

K. V. Sarma (1919–2005) worked in Indology and history. He studied under V. A. Ramaswami Sastri at University College Thiruvananthapuram and the University of Kerala, later holding posts at Panjab University, the VVRI, and the Adyar Library and Research Centre.

K. Venkata Ramanan worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Peking University under Yongtong Tang and Sentian Wang, and under Prabodh Chandra Bagchi at Visva-Bharati University, where he also taught; he was later a visiting scholar at the Harvard-Yenching Institute.
Kaigen Noritake (born 1952) specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Kenyu Mitomo and served as an assistant professor at Rissho University (attested 2007).

Kaikyoku Watanabe (1872–1933) worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Jōdo Shūgaku Honkō and the University of Strasbourg under Ernst Leumann, and held professorships at Shukyo, Toyo, Kokushikan, and Taisho Universities, alongside heading Shiba Junior & Senior High.

Kaiten Nukariya (1867–1934) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar. Educated at Komazawa, Keio, and First Higher School, he lectured at Harvard (~1913–1915) and served as professor and first president of Komazawa University (1925–1934).
Kaiun Shirodate is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He taught at Otani University, where he was attested as a lecturer from 1986 to 1990 and as a professor from 1999 to 2002.

Kakichi Kadowaki (1926–2017) was a scholar of religious studies, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1948–1952), studied under Sogen Omori, and held a post at Sophia University from around 1969 to 1996.

Kakushō Ujiie (died 1985) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He carried out research study at Tribhuvan University (attested 1970) and served as a professor at Koyasan University (attested 1970 and 1984–1985).

Kali Kinkar Datta (1905–1982) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He served at Patna University, where he was attested as Vice-Chancellor in 1973, and as Honorary Director and Joint Director of the K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute.

Kalidas Nag (1891–1966) was an Indology, history, and archaeology scholar. He studied at Scottish Church College and the University of Calcutta, where he later held posts (~1914–1919 and ~1923–1955), and served as General Secretary of The Asiatic Society (~1942–1946).
Kalpana K. Sheth is a scholar of Indology who completed doctoral studies under Harivallabh Chunilal Bhayani and held a post at the Lalbhai Dalpatbhai Institute of Indology.

Kalu Rinpoche (1905–1989) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure. He studied at Palpung Monastery and Dechen Osel Ling under Khakyab Dorje, Situ Pema Wangchok Gyalpo, and Lama Norbu Dondrup, later serving as Palpung's Vajra Master and abbot of Changchub Choeling.

Kalyan Kumar Sarkar is a scholar of Indology, history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied under Prabodh Chandra Bagchi and became an emeritus professor at the University of Windsor (attested 2002).

Kamala Tiyavanich is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. She studied at Cornell University under David K. Wyatt, A. Thomas Kirsch, and Richard Polenberg, and held a Mellon Postdoctoral Fellowship there in 1993–1994.
Kamaleswar Bhattacharya (1928–2014) was a scholar in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies who held academic posts at Brown University, the University of Toronto, and the University of Bonn.
